coaching.headline: Skylar's 17 kills and 61,612 damage to heroes could not cover it: Bayle's 8 offlane deaths and Morigesh's fights skipped alive at 20.9 and 30.5 sank the game anyway.
coaching.team: The carry matchup ran to Kira all game while the duo lane read was even, with two duo deaths on each side before minute 10, but Skylar's damage covered for it late: 61,612 to heroes and 17 kills. The offlane never got to lane: Bayle ran unfavored against Aurora, and Scarlett's jungle killed him five separate times. The Fangtooth fight at 19.1 was a 5v4 in our favor and still went 2-4 — the team had the man advantage and lost it anyway. The Inner Tower fight at 20.9 went 0-3, with Morigesh and Greystone both alive and never in it. We won the fights at 22.9 and 25.2, taking their Outer Tower and trading a Fangtooth along the way. Towers kept falling anyway, and the 30.5 Inhibitor fight repeated 19.1 exactly: 5v4, lost 2-4. River control finished 7-15, towers 3-11. Next game: when the numbers favor us, take the fight and finish it — don't lose the 5v4.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: Two 5-vs-4 fights, at 19.1 for Fangtooth and 30.5 for the Inhibitor, were both lost anyway — 2-4 both times — despite the extra body. The 20.9 Inner Tower loss compounded it: Morigesh and Greystone were both alive and never joined a fight that went 0-3.
coaching.whatWorked: Skylar's damage: 61,612 to heroes and 17 kills carried every fight the team won, including the 3-1 conversion at their Outer Tower at 22.9.

perPlayer.4d74281b-efff-4eac-a187-bdac28f9958d: Morigesh's one kill and two deaths look clean, but she sat out two of the costliest fights alive: the Inner Tower loss at 20.9 (0-3) and the Inhibitor loss at 30.5 (2-4 despite a 5v4 edge). Her build skipped two winning-core items, Lifebinder and Megacosm.
perPlayer.546c8f8c-ffd5-4c3b-9d42-b079ba8c4a2f: Greystone put up 10 assists and led the team in objective damage at 16,174, but died five times and built zero armor into a comp that ran three-fifths physical — the matchup flag the engine raised directly. He was also one of two players alive and absent from the lost 20.9 Inner Tower fight.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Steel held 76% kill participation and a team-high 63,858 damage mitigated, doing the frontline job the lane needed, with a team-high 16 assists. He was caught alone by Kira at 7.1 — the same solo-catch habit flagged in his last three films is still showing up.
perPlayer.fc72f14e-5424-4f4a-b271-519e2eda81a7: Bayle lost the offlane matchup to Aurora the whole game and paid for it eight times, the most deaths on the team; Scarlett's jungle alone accounted for five of those kills. He also placed zero wards and built none of the three winning-core items, Overlord, Rapture or Cursed Scroll.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Skylar was the only real offense on the roster: 17 kills, 61,612 damage to heroes, more than double the next-highest total. The carry matchup itself ran to Kira all game, and a solo catch by valmont at 26.8 cost the Inhibitor and Inner Tower soon after — the one blemish on an otherwise dominant night.

19.1.call: We had a 5v4 man advantage at their Fangtooth and still went 2-4 — that's a fight to win, not one to just show up to.

20.9.call: Our Inner Tower fell after we lost this fight 0-3 while Morigesh and Greystone stood alive and never joined; five bodies there and the count is different.

22.9.call: The fight at their Outer Tower went 3-1 and took the tower — proof the team could win the objective trade when everyone showed up.

30.5.call: Same story as 19.1: a 5v4 lead at the Inhibitor, and it still went 2-4. Two man-advantage fights lost the same way is the pattern to fix.

ranking.grade: 17 kills, 6 deaths, 61,612 damage to heroes — nearly triple the next-best total.
Steel: 76% kill participation, 16 assists, 63,858 damage mitigated — held the frontline all game.
Greystone: 10 assists, 16,174 objective damage — but zero armor and 5 deaths.
Morigesh: fewest deaths on the team, but alive and absent from the 20.9 loss.
Bayle: 8 deaths, the most on the team; 5 of them to Scarlett alone.

4d74281b-efff-4eac-a187-bdac28f9958d.build: Morigesh skipped the winning core's Lifebinder and Megacosm, both sustain-and-scaling mage items, for Overseer's vision and Amulet of Chaos's early burst instead — a bet on early trading over the late-game power the winning 45.2% core banks on, which shows up in her modest 19,211 damage to heroes.
4d74281b-efff-4eac-a187-bdac28f9958d.eternal: Vesh fits Morigesh because Mark, Hive and Curse are all ability hits that Vesh turns into added damage-over-time, rewarding her ability-power mage build over a burst-item alternative.

546c8f8c-ffd5-4c3b-9d42-b079ba8c4a2f.build: Greystone kept Overlord but skipped Augmentation and Basilisk, the winning core's two armor-and-tankiness pieces, for Sky Splitter, Necrosis and Ashbringer instead — pure damage, and zero armor into a comp that ran three-fifths physical, the matchup flag the engine raised directly.
546c8f8c-ffd5-4c3b-9d42-b079ba8c4a2f.eternal: Thraex fits Greystone's stick-and-trade jungle kit by marking the last hero he hits to swing the damage trade in his favor, though it does nothing for the missing armor that let this three-fifths-physical comp punish him.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Steel built two of three core items, Xenia and Dynamo, swapping Gaia Greaves' armor for Tainted Guard and Prophecy against a three-fifths-physical comp. His team-high 63,858 damage mitigated says it still held up.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: The engine doesn't model support Eternals like Exarch, Weald or Marrow, so there's no fit read for Steel here beyond noting the field mostly runs a peel-first major on frontline supports like this.

fc72f14e-5424-4f4a-b271-519e2eda81a7.build: Bayle built none of the winning core's three items, Overlord, Rapture or Cursed Scroll, running Manta Scythe, Salvation, Draconum and Tainted Blade instead — a full off-core build against a matchup that was already unfavored, with Scarlett free to punish it five separate times.
fc72f14e-5424-4f4a-b271-519e2eda81a7.eternal: Thraex fits Bayle's all-in duelist kit the same way, marking his target to swing the trade once Berserk kicks in below 40% health, though it does nothing for the five separate Scarlett ganks that never let the duel start.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Skylar built the full winning core, Plasma Blade, Vanquisher and Imperator, then added Terminus and Tainted Rounds on top — on core, nothing to teach here.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Vermis fits Skylar's on-hit kite-and-shoot kit, dealing bonus max-health damage on repeated hits to the same target, matching the 17-kill night she put together.

threats: Chain-CC risk (3 hard-CC abilities, ~2.5s of lockdown): Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Riktor. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 4 items of it.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Bayle Kingslayer (knockback). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Steel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Mark a target → Hive slow → Swarm reposition → Curse execute-burst ult
ourKits.winCondition: Mark + Curse a squishy and delete them with %max-HP Pestilence
ourKits.playWith: setup that holds her marked target
ourKits.playAgainst: she's squishy with one escape (Swarm) — dive after it's used; spread vs Hive

ourKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap → Make Way armor shred → Sacred Oath empowered basic → Stone Forged Soul stasis ult
ourKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
ourKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
ourKits.playAgainst: don't waste burst into his stasis — wait it out; anti-heal cuts the ult heal

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
ourKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
ourKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
ourKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

ourKits.combo: Skull Crusher gap-close → Dire Howl slow → Cursed Edge → Kingslayer knockback dash, Berserk at low HP
ourKits.winCondition: engage, drop low into Berserk and out-brawl
ourKits.playWith: follow-up while he commits the dive
ourKits.playAgainst: his Berserk rewards low HP — burst him fully or disengage; anti-heal helps

ourKits.combo: Plasma Grenade → Hypercharge on-hit → Air Assault reposition → Atomiser ult
ourKits.winCondition: Hypercharge and kite-shoot from Air Assault safety
ourKits.passive: extra jump; kills cause corpse explosions
ourKits.playWith: a frontline so she can free-fire airborne
ourKits.playAgainst: CC her out of Air Assault; she's squishy on the ground

enemyKits.combo: Riplash pull → Shock Therapy silence → Skewer suppress ult
enemyKits.winCondition: pull a target in and chain silence+suppress for a guaranteed kill
enemyKits.playWith: burst that deletes his pulled/suppressed target
enemyKits.playAgainst: respect Riplash range — stay spaced; cleanse/QSS the suppress

enemyKits.combo: Mercy poke → stack Vengeance → Shadow Glide reposition → Purge ult
enemyKits.winCondition: stack Vengeance and shred with the channeled Purge
enemyKits.playWith: peel so she can channel Purge safely
enemyKits.playAgainst: interrupt/CC her during Purge; punish her short dash cooldown

enemyKits.combo: Boreal Sweep slow → Hoarfrost root → Glacial Charge engage → Cryoseism stun ult
enemyKits.winCondition: chain frost CC (slow→root→stun) to lock the fight down
enemyKits.playWith: burst that converts her long CC chain into kills
enemyKits.playAgainst: she's a CC battery — cleanse/QSS the Cryoseism stun; spread to avoid the chain
